ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, franchise master franchisee background and royalty payment counterparties against the Gibraltar Sanctions Notice list, United Kingdom Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) consolidated list, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list and the United States OFAC SDN list. A risk-based Politically Exposed Person (PEP) check is required, with enhanced due diligence for PEPs, Chinese state-affiliated officials, state-owned enterprise shareholders and any beneficial owner who cannot produce a clean and verifiable source of funds. Screening must be completed before incorporation filing and refreshed every six months or upon any material change to the structural holding chain.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Gibraltar Companies Registry e-Services portal (Companies House Gibraltar)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be in English using Latin script; a Chinese trading name may appear only as a parallel non-statutory translation. The name must be distinguishable from all existing Gibraltar registered companies; no public deception, no similarity to a protected brand, and no use of words suggesting the patronage of Her Majesty or any foreign government.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Gibraltar Companies Registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant or its licensed registered agent may file a written administrative appeal with the Registry's Registrar within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must state the grounds of distinction from existing registrations, disclose why the proposed name is not prohibited or misleading, and enclose the original name rejection letter together with supporting evidence of lexical availability. If the Registrar does not overturn the rejection within 10 working days, the applicant may request conciliation through the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission Adjudication Unit or a further judicial review in the Gibraltar Supreme Court. During the appeal period, a fresh name reservation may be filed under a different proposed name; the original 30-day reservation window does not toll.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office can be accepted by the Gibraltar Companies Registry for statutory registered office purposes for an exempted holding vehicle only where the service provider is licensed and the registered office is not used as the public-facing trading address. For the Chinese malatang fast-casual self-serve broth bowl master licensing business, a physical licensed premises in Gibraltar will be required for any local operations, while a virtual office may be used for the holding company and royalty collection platform. Full business licensing substance must exist before operational transactions commence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium — quantified 36% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months because the fast-casual franchise model combines registered office substance, local food preparation premises and royalty wire rails which attract Business Licensing Authority and GFSC contagion monitoring.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Bermuda Companies Act 1981, ss. 6 (incorporation), 14C (exempted company), 18 and 25 (share capital), 70 (registered office), 74 (directors), 82 (secretary) and 95 (annual validation); such company also registers as an external company in Gibraltar under Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, ss. 301-310.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda, Financial and Corporate Registry, 36 Victoria Street, Hamilton HM 12, Bermuda; for Gibraltar external registration: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, 6-8 Europort, Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form CO-14C (Application for Registration as an Exempted Company) under the Bermuda Companies Act 1981, followed by Form EX-1 (Notice of External Company Registration) filed with the Gibraltar Companies Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A Bermuda exempted company is required to have an authorized share capital of at least USD 12,000 or its equivalent; one subscriber share of par value must be issued and fully paid prior to registration. No escrow account is required by law for paid-up capital; a statement of capital and a declaration of solvency are filed with the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the Bermuda Exempted Company’s Memorandum of Association and Bye-laws, as presented and filed with the Registrar of Companies, Bermuda, are approved and adopted. RESOLVED: That each subscriber share, being one ordinary share of USD 0.01 par value set out in the Statement of Capital, is allotted and issued fully paid, free of escrow. RESOLVED: That the registered office be fixed at the address of the registered office agent in Hamilton, Bermuda, and statutory registers be opened there. RESOLVED: That [Director A] and [Director B] are appointed first directors and [Secretary C] first company secretary. RESOLVED: That the directors and secretary are authorized to register the company as an external company in Gibraltar and to execute all applications required for trade, food safety, fire safety, and environmental licensing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Approval and Exempted Status Assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Financial and Corporate Registry, Hamilton, Bermuda (e-Registration portal available).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search through the Bermuda Registry’s online index. Submit a name reservation request confirming the name ends with 'Limited'; confirm the proposed name contains no restricted words under s.13 of the Companies Act 1981; obtain a provisional name approval. Simultaneously engage a licensed registered agent to support the exempted company application and provide confirmation that the company will carry on business outside Bermuda.
required_dossiers: Certificate of good standing or licence of the proposed registered agent
Proposed Memorandum of Association and draft Bye-laws
Identity documents of subscribers and proposed directors
Written confirmation that the business will be conducted outside Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried on grounds of distinctiveness or sensitive words, file a written representation to the Registrar within 14 days and submit an alternative name for accelerated re-check at no additional assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public authorized by the Supreme Court of Bermuda.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the Memorandum of Association and Bye-laws with an authorized capital clause of at least USD 12,000 divided into shares of par value not less than USD 0.01. Ensure each subscriber executes the subscriber pages before a notary. Prepare the registered office consent signed by the licensed registered agent. Obtain sworn declarations from the first directors confirming fitness, residence status, and solvency.
required_dossiers: Statement of Authorized Capital and Initial Shareholdings
Consent to act of registered office holder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or Registrar identifies a technical defect in execution, re-execute the relevant signature pages and obtain fresh notarial certification within five working days; if the capital clause is defective, file an amended Statement of Capital with the return.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration as Bermuda Exempted Company and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (Companies and e-Registry Department, Hamilton).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Form CO-14C together with notarized constitutional documents and supporting declarations. Pay the registry incorporation fee in Bermudian dollars by bank transfer or e-payment. The Registrar examines the statutory compliance, endorses the exempted status, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation and an accompanying certificate of exempted company status.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association and Bye-laws
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query under the Companies Act 1981, rectify the discrepancy in capital, directors, or registered office particulars within 21 days; if the file is closed, re-submit with a new application and the applicable late-filing administrative charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Corporate Governance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First directors and company secretary acting through the Bermuda registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene and hold the first board meeting by written resolution. Allocate the subscriber shares; adopt the Statutory Register and Register of Members; open the Beneficial Ownership Register under the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership Act 2017; appoint the officers; authorize the opening of bank accounts and the filing of the Gibraltar external company registration. Issue share certificates to the subscribers and maintain minutes in the corporate books.
required_dossiers: Register of Members and Register of Directors
Consents to act of directors and secretary
Minutes of the first board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any officer fails to consent, appoint a replacement by a subsequent board circular resolution and file an amended officer notice with the Bermuda Registry; late beneficial ownership filings are cured by filing a corrected late return and paying the fixed penalty.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory with fiscal autonomy. Direct taxes are administered by the Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (Commissioner of Income Tax), official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi/income-tax-office. Indirect taxes (VAT and customs) are administered by HM Customs & Excise Department (Commissioner of Customs and VAT), official portal: https://www.customs.gov.gi. Governing statutes: Income Tax Act 2010 (as amended) and Value Added Tax Act 2019 (Gibraltar).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the foreign Bermuda Exempted Company with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies either as an oversea company establishing a branch/place of business or by incorporating a Gibraltar subsidiary/branch vehicle. Step 2: Apply to the Income Tax Office for the Gibraltar corporate TIN by submitting the branch/corporate registration form, certified copies of the Bermuda certificate of incorporation, the Bermuda Tax Exemption Certificate, constitutional documents, board resolutions, audited financials, and evidence that central management and control remain outside Gibraltar for non-resident classification. Step 3: Apply to HM Customs & Excise Department for VAT registration when taxable turnover exceeds GIP 150,000, or before the first taxable supply if the supplier is not established in Gibraltar; voluntary VAT registration is permitted. Step 4: Appoint a Gibraltar-resident tax representative and provide local registered address, bank details, and forecast turnover. Step 5: Receive the Gibraltar VAT identification number (GI prefix) and the Income Tax TIN, then file annual corporate tax returns and periodic VAT returns through the official electronic portals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Bermuda Exempted Company holding a Tax Exemption Certificate issued under the Exempted Companies Act 1981; however, Gibraltar does not recognise the Bermuda tax exemption and will treat the entity as a non-resident company subject to entity-level territorial taxation of Gibraltar-source profits only, at the Gibraltar corporation tax rate of 12.5%; no pass-through status is available in Gibraltar).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no US-style check-the-box or pass-through election. Available statutory elections: (1) election to be treated as ordinarily resident in Gibraltar where central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar; (2) voluntary VAT registration election under the Value Added Tax Act 2019 for sub-threshold taxable persons; (3) group registration and group relief elections under the Income Tax Act 2010; (4) group reconstruction and loss surrender elections for qualifying Gibraltar groups; (5) renewal of the Bermuda Tax Exemption Certificate as a statutory annual election; (6) documentation and disclosure elections addressing OECD BEPS Action 2 hybrid mismatch outcomes, including alignment of disregarded franchise payment positions to prevent double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act 2019, administered by HM Customs & Excise Department; structurally aligned with UK VAT principles but outside the EU VAT territory and outside UK mainland VAT jurisdiction.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GIP 150,000 (Gibraltar Pounds, pegged 1:1 to GBP) of taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period; nil threshold for non-established foreign suppliers, who must register before making their first taxable supply in Gibraltar; voluntary registration available for below-threshold businesses.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory B2B or B2G electronic invoicing, no continuous transaction controls, and no digital stamping regime is currently in force in Gibraltar. Taxpayers must issue VAT-compliant invoices within statutory deadlines, retain records (digital or paper) for six years, and file VAT returns electronically with HM Customs & Excise Department. UK Making Tax Digital obligations do not attach to Gibraltar-only VAT registrations but will apply if the enterprise separately holds a UK VAT registration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for: (a) goods physically exported from Gibraltar to destinations outside Gibraltar, including packaged take-away food consignments exported by the supplier, whereas dine-in Malatang self-serve servings remain standard-rated; (b) zero-rated food categories listed in the Gibraltar VAT schedule, notably cold self-serve food for off-premises consumption when not supplied in the course of catering; (c) services directly connected to exported goods; and (d) franchise master-licence royalties, brand licence fees, and management charges supplied to non-Gibraltar franchisees, which are outside the scope of Gibraltar VAT (or zero-rated) where the effective use and enjoyment of the intellectual property occurs outside Gibraltar. All claims require documented proof of export, destination, counterparty status, and payment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Gibraltar Customs Export Declaration (Electronic SAD/C88 or equivalent lodged through the Gibraltar customs electronic portal)
Commercial Invoice and signed Export Contract
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR note, or courier Proof of Delivery with destination-country customs stamps
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Franchise royalty computation, IP licence agreement, and effective-use-and-enjoyment evidence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HM Customs & Excise Department may open audits within six years, extended where fraud or wilful default is evidenced, and may issue best-judgment assessments retrospectively clawing back zero-rated VAT, interest, and penalties. Civil penalties reach up to 100% of the VAT evaded for fraudulent evasion, with fixed penalties for failure to obtain or retain export evidence; criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment of up to seven years, unlimited fines, director disqualification, and seizure of exported goods. The burden is on the supplier to prove physical export and repatriation of proceeds within the obligatory 180-day period; any false or fabricated export documentation is treated as fraudulent evasion and invalidates all refund claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (Sterling monetary authority), H.M. Treasury (UK financial sanctions and exchange-control policy), and the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (licensing, AML/CFT and banking supervision in Gibraltar).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar applies no separate foreign-exchange-control regime for current or capital account transactions. Sterling, US dollars, and euros may be freely received, held and remitted without central-bank approval. Capital account transactions and profit remittances are unrestricted for a non-resident Bermuda Exempted Company, provided that the underlying transaction does not touch sanctioned jurisdictions or Parties and that bank-level compliance receives complete source-of-funds evidence. The practical hurdles are anti-money-laundering due diligence and economic-substance documentation; corporate payments into mainland China must also comply with PRC SAFE administration purpose codes and the foreign beneficiary's withholding/currency declaration, but no Gibraltar-side surrender or conversion approval applies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio exist in Gibraltar for export proceeds, royalty receipts, or franchise fees. The Exchange Control Act 1947 as historically applied to Gibraltar has not been used to require conversion into Sterling; entities may retain 100% of foreign-currency receipts in original or freely convertible currencies. Where the receivable is sourced from mainland China, the Chinese paying entity remains subject to PRC exchange-control verification at the point of remittance, but the Gibraltar receiving account has no surrender obligation and no deadline beyond ordinary bank credit validation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium for a Bermuda Exempted Company operating in Gibraltar. A UK or EEA electronic-money institution is not passport-provisionable into Gibraltar after Brexit; offering e-money or payment-account services inside Gibraltar without a Gibraltar Financial Services Commission licence would contravene Gibraltar's Financial Services (Electronic Money) Act and Payment Services Act. An offshore EMI may be used only as an ancillary collection/disbursement sub-ledger outside the Gibraltar licensed perimeter and must never be presented to franchisees as a bank account. The capital escrow and main operating treasury should be held with a GFSC-licensed bank; any digital EMI funds must be segregated and legally incapable of being used for lending.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no statutory rule that every director must appear physically in Gibraltar; however, GFSC AML/CFT Guidance expects banks to identify and verify directors and beneficial owners. In practice, at least one senior director or a designated beneficial owner should attend a video interview with the compliance team and, where the bank's risk appetite demands, complete a physical signing/closing meeting in Gibraltar or before a recognized notary public. Remote onboarding is viable for high-quality structures, but a Bermuda Exempted Company with non-resident Chinese owners will trigger additional evidence of physical presence so the bank can document genuine substance and nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership located in mainland China with a foodservice franchisor structure, creating source-of-wealth opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised passports and PRC Identity Cards, corporate registry transcript of all intermediate holding companies, Gibraltar and Bermuda certificates of incorporation, register of directors and members, audited annual financial statements of the ultimate shareholder and corporate group, three years of personal and corporate bank statements showing accumulation of wealth, tax residence certificates, source-of-wealth memorandum, and independent professional references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda Exempted Company with no office, employees, or economic substance in Gibraltar, while requesting a Gibraltar bank account and cross-border royalty flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Gibraltar registered office and licensed corporate services provider agreement, executed board resolutions and minutes held in Gibraltar, economic substance notification and supporting calculations, expected local payroll, lease, IT or management expenditure, franchise-related IP and original contracts, and a clear business plan demonstrating that treasury, licensing, contract administration and dispute management functions are managed from Gibraltar.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive Chinese fast-casual restaurant franchise operation, raising AML concerns despite the Low_Risk_Standard rating.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original master franchise and area-development agreements, uniform accounting and POS system description for self-serve broth counters, royalty calculation file, sales and royalty audits, trademark and trade-name registrations, PRC food business licence and hygienic permits, downstream franchisee KYC extract where relevant, and tax and wiring declarations showing that royalty wires are not connected to cash-processing risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or repatriation red flags due to routing of RMB-denominated franchise royalties from mainland China through multiple correspondent banks to Gibraltar.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: HMT and OFAC sanctions screening policy with negative-hit records, counterparty and franchisee restricted-party check, payment-trace descriptor showing contractual reference and withholding, constitutional and beneficial-ownership declaration, transfer-pricing file for the royalty arrangement, and any applicable Chinese withholding tax, VAT, fapiao or SAFE filings demonstrating the cross-border nature of each payment.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound equity or shareholder loans from the ultimate owner into the Gibraltar or Bermuda treasury account, route by SWIFT gpi MT103 rather than MT202 where each payment contains the bank-confirmed reference such as 'Share Capital Contribution' or 'Subordinated Shareholder Loan ref [agreement number]'; use the originating State's purpose code for direct investment or intercompany financing, accompanied by an executed board resolution, share certificate issuance transcript, loan agreement and source-of-funds letter. The beneficiary bank will verify corresponding SWIFT field 50K or ultimate originator, 57D beneficiary bank, and 70 remittance details against the entity's account mandate; any CHAPS Sterling settlement into the Gibraltar account must be denominated in GBP with a same-day value date and a written confirmation of the underlying capital transaction. No Gibraltar declaration form is mandatory, but the bank will retain the full transaction file for at least six years.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settle verified trade payables and franchise supplier invoices through SWIFT gpi MT103 as open-account disbursements, or with an irrevocable commercial letter of credit issued under SWIFT MT700 and subject to UCP600 for equipment and ingredient imports. For RMB suppliers in mainland China, use pre-funded CNH clearing through Hong Kong clearing banks or CIPS RMB direct participation, quoting the underlying contract number in field 70; for commodity-style purchases, use documentary collection DP/DA instructions if the letter of credit is not commercially efficient. The bank will retain purchase orders, invoices, bills of lading, import customs declarations and translations as the evidential file; if the recipient is a related party, the payment must be supported by transfer pricing documentation and Local_POS reconciliation to prove that disbursements are not disguised capital flight.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable GBP/CNY and USD/GBP forwards for firm and forecast royalty exposures
Offshore RMB non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for Chinese renminbi receipts where onshore deliverability is unavailable to a non-PRC entity
Cross-currency swaps (GBP/USD/CNH) under an ISDA/CSA entered into with a licensed Gibraltar or UK bank
FX swaps and rollovers for treasury liquidity matching of escrow and operational accounts
Plain-vanilla over-the-counter options for currency risk on committed franchise expansion capex, subject to the bank's derivatives-policy approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Return and Government Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January each year in respect of the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a 10% monthly penalty, subject to deregistration of the exempted company after continued default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry, HM Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of registration of the overseas company in Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of GIP 50 per month; continued default triggers administrative strike-off, disqualification of directors, and personal liability for fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System (BOSS), Registrar of Companies, Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the filing of the annual return; or within 30 days after any transfer or change of beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal offence with maximum fine of GIP 20,000 and/or imprisonment not exceeding 2 years; daily default fines may apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Environmental Health Department / Business Licensing Office, HM Government of Gibraltar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal on or before 31 March of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating without a current licence is a continuing offence carrying daily fines of up to GIP 5,000 and a closure order.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent annual audit is mandatory unless the company qualifies for small-company audit exemption by satisfying at least two of the following: annual turnover not exceeding GIP 1,000,000; balance-sheet total not exceeding GIP 500,000; average employees not exceeding 50. A Gibraltar-registered overseas company must also deliver audited accounts if parent or consolidated turnover exceeds applicable group thresholds.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as endorsed by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission; Bermuda exempted companies may file accounts prepared in accordance with IFRS or acceptable local GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All shareholding transfers and changes in beneficial ownership must be entered in the statutory register and, for Gibraltar purposes, submitted to BOSS within 30 days. Even in the absence of any transfer, a nil annual confirmation is required on the anniversary date of the annual return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Gibraltar registered office and corporate agent fees typically range from USD 1,200 to USD 4,500 per annum; Bermuda registered office charges range from USD 1,000 to USD 3,500 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: For a low-volume master-licensing entity, certified audit fees typically range from USD 3,000 to USD 12,000 per annum depending on transaction volume and consolidation complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% (flat rate applicable to Gibraltar tax-resident companies and to Gibraltar permanent establishments of non-resident persons under the Income Tax Act 2010; the Bermuda Exempted Company head office remains exempt in Bermuda on its foreign-source income).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No Gibraltar tax holidays, patent box or preferential IP deductions are available. Reliefs include the Gibraltar participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains from substantial shareholdings, unilateral foreign tax credit relief, and capital allowances on plant and machinery. Gibraltar remains outside the EU VAT area; no VAT/GST is charged. The 12.5% rate is a single-headline commercial rate for all trades, including fast-casual franchise licensing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: GRA Company Income Tax Return (Form CT-100) filed electronically through the Gibraltar Revenue Authority (GRA) eTax portal; a separate annual confirmation is filed with the Gibraltar Companies House under the Companies Act 2006.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Self-assessment filing and final corporation tax payment are due no later than six months after the end of the accounting period (e.g. 30 June for a 31 December year-end). The chargeable period is the year of assessment in which the accounting period ends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, Gibraltar tax reference number (TRN) and Unique Identification Number (UIN).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Bermuda Exempted Company legal name, its Gibraltar branch UIN and the TRN issued upon registration of the Gibraltar permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period starting and ending dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the exact financial year period of the Bermuda Exempted Company that coincides with the Gibraltar branch accounts; align with Companies House annual return dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Turnover and gross receipts, excluding any non-taxable capital items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Gibraltar-source franchise revenue, self-serve broth bowl sales, POS collections and master licence income apportioned to the Gibraltar branch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductible expenses claimed under the Income Tax Act 2010 (wholly and exclusively incurred).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only branch-allocated costs; management charges from the Bermuda parent must satisfy the arm's-length principle and be supported by invoices and economic substance evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted trading profit after add-backs and disallowable expenditure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back depreciation, non-deductible entertainment and any Bermuda head office overhead not incurred for the Gibraltar trade; attach a branch profit allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital allowances, losses brought forward, double tax relief and total tax payable at 12.5%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, the Gibraltar tax residence certificate and loss carry-forward computations where applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed penalty of up to GIP 5,000 plus a daily default penalty of up to GIP 50 per day after GRA notice. Deliberate non-compliance can trigger a further penalty of up to 100% of the tax due. Late-paid tax carries interest at 10% per annum from the due date until settlement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — Gibraltar does not impose a withholding tax on dividends paid by a Gibraltar tax-resident company or by the Gibraltar permanent establishment of a non-resident company. No advance corporation tax or dividend withholding mechanism exists under the Income Tax Act 2010.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No income tax treaty exists between Gibraltar and Bermuda. Where a UK corporate parent is interposed, the United Kingdom–Gibraltar Double Taxation Agreement may apply; a Gibraltar tax residence certificate (TRC) is issued by the GRA upon application and must accompany the dividend claim. Because the Bermuda Exempted Company has no DTA protection, reliance rests entirely on Gibraltar's domestic 0% withholding regime, supported by board resolutions, beneficial ownership declarations and economic substance records evidencing that the Exempted Company is the genuine recipient.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory withholding tax on cross-border IP royalties paid by a Gibraltar payer; no treaty reduction is required. Interest: 0% statutory withholding tax on arm's-length interest paid to corporate non-residents. Both payments remain subject to the arm's-length standard and must be commercially benchmarked to withstand a transfer pricing adjustment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: GIP 100,000 de minimis compliance threshold for related-party cross-border transactions (royalty, management fee or license payments) used as the internal documentation trigger; Country-by-Country reporting and notification apply only to MNE groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Fully applicable. Gibraltar's Economic Substance Regulations require any tax-resident company or Gibraltar PE carrying on a relevant activity — including franchise licensing, distribution, holding of IP, and intra-group financing — to demonstrate management and control in Gibraltar, adequate physical premises, proportionate full-time employees and local expenditure. A Bermuda Exempted Company managed from Gibraltar or trading through a Gibraltar PE must hold board meetings in Gibraltar, maintain local books and payroll, and keep core income-generating activities within the jurisdiction. Failure to satisfy the test allows the GRA to reallocate the Bermuda entity's profits into the taxable Gibraltar branch and to apply sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming Bermuda tax exemption while directing the Chinese malatang self-serve franchise operations from Gibraltar and failing to declare Gibraltar-source trading profit and royalty income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Income Tax Act 2010 (Gibraltar), a penalty of up to 100% of the tax undercharged, plus interest at 10% per annum, civil recovery proceedings in the Supreme Court of Gibraltar, public restitution orders and strike-off by the Registrar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the Bermuda Exempted Company face civil restitution, disqualification under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2006, court-imposed travel bans and imprisonment of up to 7 years on indictment for fraudulent evasion of tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Holding the master licence and royalty rights in the Bermuda Exempted Company without employees, premises, board minutes or core income-generating activity in either Bermuda or Gibraltar, and receiving passive royalty income with no local substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under the Gibraltar Economic Substance Regulations of up to GIP 100,000, direction to file corrective returns, reallocation of all royalty income into the taxable Gibraltar branch, and removal of the company from the Gibraltar register upon persistent non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors incur personal financial penalties for failure to make economic substance filings; continued violations lead to disqualification orders, freezing injunctions over overseas assets and potential extradition proceedings where dishonesty is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Food Establishment / Consumer Health Violation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the self-serve broth bowl outlet without the statutory Gibraltar food business registration, environmental health inspection and fast-casual food premise licence required for ISIC 5610 activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Immediate closure notice by the environmental health authority, fines of up to GIP 20,000 per day of unlicensed trading, revocation of ancillary licences and civil damages to franchisees for misrepresentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for enforcement costs; wilful non-compliance can result in 12 months' imprisonment, permanent prohibition from acting as directors and restitution orders for consumer losses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing And AML / Sanctions Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting a non-arm's-length royalty for the 'Chinese Malatang Self-Serve Master Brand' payable to the Bermuda Exempted Company, omitting contemporaneous benchmark documentation, or routing payments to a franchisee or related party subject to financial sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment to taxable profits, a penalty of up to 50% of the adjustment plus interest, mandatory reporting to the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission, confiscation of prohibited payments and adverse public registry notation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable under Gibraltar anti-money laundering and sanctions legislation, with travel restrictions, employment prohibitions, personal fines and imprisonment of up to 7 years under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 (Gibraltar).
